It's not always clear to me how different versions of Lean, subverso and verso need to interact. In my project, I have a Lean/ folder and a Verso/ folder, where the Lean/ folder is (currently) on v4.28.0, and has a subverso dependency and contains files which have ANCHOR tags, and the Verso/ folder is on v4.26.0-rc1, and also has a subverso dependency (with no-modules), and I know that these two Lean versions don't need to match. But I'm getting errors from subverso, which I suspect is because of the verso version being wrong. It worked before I bumped the Lean/ folder from some v4.25-rc. Is there a clear explanation of what needs to match, and what doesn't need to match?
I know that the Lean versions between the thing running verso and the example files don't need to match, and that the versions of subverso do need to match, but that's about it right now.

You're right - the Lean versions don't need to match, but the examples do need the same version of SubVerso. Generally, they should be pointed at the same SHA hash in lake-manifest.json (I usually have a little script to double-check this in my CI). If the two versions straddle the module system introduction, then there's slightly different setup to arrange that each gets the correct version (with/without module system), but these versions should both be using the module system.

Which errors are you getting?

I have since fixed this, but I don't completely understand why it failed in the first place. The commit that broke things was https://github.com/b-mehta/Polychromatic/commit/0b998a71738affe9f92da13178fe1eec10e57711#diff-60d88684d9a9c25126ffeea4d087f09339d2c53b05adbdf3abcaee690ed8bb02, with error logs here https://github.com/b-mehta/Polychromatic/actions/runs/22754347161/job/65995371920#step:5:21. Bumping the subverso version fixed it: https://github.com/b-mehta/Polychromatic/pull/70/changes

The way SubVerso maintains compatibility with Every Lean Release Ever is through metaprogramming, rather than maintaining a ton of branches. The module SubVerso.Compatdefines a compatibility layer, and it needs updating for new Lean releases.

The error that you were seeing came from updating to a Lean version that had replaced String.Pos as a wrapper around bytes with String.Pos s as a byte index paired with a proof of validity in s. The update skipped the deprecation cycle completely, leading to that type error. Updating SubVerso also brought in the fixed compatibility layer that papers over the string API differences.

Going one version at a time would have at least given a deprecation message, but bumping SubVerso is still going to be necessary.

Ah! That makes total sense - SubVerso is compatible with every lean release, but has no hope of doing so for lean releases from its future, so the mistake was in bumping lean without bumping subverso to a version which was aware of that version of Lean. Thanks!

I'm trying to update a project that was on Mathlib's 4.29.0 tag to the 4.30.0 tag, and for which I have a verso manual, and I have weird errors that I don't understand and I can't get the verso manual to compile.
The bump PR is https://github.com/LeanMachineLearning/LML/pull/114, and the error can be seen at https://github.com/LeanMachineLearning/LML/actions/runs/27057619081/job/79864752901. The error message is enormous and gets truncated in that view: I don't know where to find a meaningful line in the message.
The main repository is a Lean project (LeanMachineLearning), and there is a folder tutorial with the verso manual in it.

I thought I could try updating subverso in the main project and/or verso in the manual subproject (the tutorial folder) but I see that they both have no tag for 4.30.0: verso has 4.29.0 and from the discussion above I get that subverso works completely differently. So I have no idea of what I should update, if anything.
Any idea of what I could try?

The lakefile of the main project is this:

name = "LeanMachineLearning"
defaultTargets = ["LeanMachineLearning"]
lintDriver = "batteries/runLinter"

[leanOptions]
pp.unicode.fun = true
autoImplicit = false
relaxedAutoImplicit = false
# Enable all mathlib linters: automatically matches what mathlib uses.
weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true

[[require]]
name = "mathlib"
git = "https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4.git"
rev = "v4.30.0"

[[require]]
name = "checkdecls"
git = "https://github.com/PatrickMassot/checkdecls.git"

[[require]]
name = "subverso"
git = "https://github.com/leanprover/subverso"

[[lean_lib]]
name = "LeanMachineLearning"

The lakefile of the tutorial verso project is this:

name = "manual"
version = "0.1.0"
keywords = ["math"]

[leanOptions]
autoImplicit = true

[[require]]
name = "verso"
git = "https://github.com/leanprover/verso"
rev = "v4.29.0"

[[lean_lib]]
name = "Manual"
root = "Manual"

[[lean_exe]]
name = "manual"
root = "Manual"

The beginning of the error I get on every code block with an anchor looks like this:

Couldn't deserialize JSON from output file: SubVerso.Highlighting.Token.kind: no inductive constructor matched
In:
{"items":
 [{"range":
   {"start": {"line": 6, "column": 1}, "end": {"line": 10, "column": 48}},
   "kind": "Lean.Parser.Module.header",
   "defines": [],
   "code": 30},
It looks to me like the version of Verso and Subverso need to be updated here - they may not have tags but a version on a more recent lean might be what you need

Thanks, updating verso in the tutorial project worked. In the end it was a very simple fix!
There is no tag release on the verso github for newer versions than 4.29.0, so I did not think about trying to update to anything newer, but its latest commits use newer toolchains and updating to the main branch fixed my problem.
Verso has tags for all the recent Lean versions, but it doesn't seem to have releases for them on GitHub.
Oh, right, sorry about the confusion. Are tags the relevant thing if I wanted to add a rev = "v4.30.0" field in a lakefile.toml?
Yes. Some context: Tags are a git feature for labeling specific commits, while releases are a GitHub feature that attaches release notes and artifacts (e.g. binaries) to a specific commit.
